label: aki_icd
citation: cohort-diff built-in definition (author-written rule).
text: Any AKI diagnosis code on the admission (ICD-10 N17.*, ICD-9 584.*).

label: aki_kdigo_48h
citation: cohort-diff built-in definition (author-written rule), after KDIGO 2012.
text: Serum creatinine rises by >= 0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours, within one admission.

label: aki_kdigo_7d
citation: cohort-diff built-in definition (author-written rule), after KDIGO 2012.
text: Serum creatinine >= 1.5 x the lowest value in the prior 7 days, within one admission.

label: dm_icd
citation: cohort-diff built-in definition (author-written rule).
text: Any diabetes diagnosis code (ICD-10 E10-E14, ICD-9 250.*).

label: dm_hba1c
citation: cohort-diff built-in definition (author-written rule).
text: Any HbA1c >= 6.5% during the admission.

label: dm_meds
citation: cohort-diff built-in definition (author-written rule).
text: Any glucose-lowering medication ordered (insulin, metformin, sulfonylureas, DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT2 inhibitors, GLP-1 agonists).

label: readmit30_any
citation: cohort-diff built-in definition (author-written rule).
text: Index admissions followed by any admission of the same patient within 30 days of discharge.

label: readmit30_excl
citation: cohort-diff built-in definition (author-written rule), inspired by CMS HRRP.
text: Index admissions followed by any admission of the same patient within 30 days of discharge, excluding index admissions ending in death, hospice or discharge against advice, and planned (elective) readmissions.

label: aki_kdigo_mimiccode
citation: Author summary of MIT-LCP mimic-code mimic-iv/concepts/organfailure/kdigo_creatinine.sql and kdigo_stages.sql (read 2026-11-04).
text: KDIGO stage >= 1 by creatinine during an ICU stay: a creatinine value is compared with the lowest value in the prior 48 hours (stage 1 if it is at least 0.3 mg/dL higher) and with the lowest value in the prior 7 days (stage 1 if it is at least 1.5 times higher). Only creatinine results from 7 days before ICU admission up to ICU discharge are used; creatinine is lab itemid 50912, values above 150 are dropped, and results at the same time are averaged.

label: aki_rahimi2023_b1
citation: Kamel Rahimi A, et al. BMC Med Inform Decis Mak. 2023;23:207. doi:10.1186/s12911-023-02306-0. Materials and methods.
text: We included patients with at least one sCr measurement on days 1, 2 and 3 following ICU admissions. We estimated AKI cases solely on the sCr criterion of the KDIGO definition defined as an increase in sCr of >= 0.3 mg/dL (26.5 umol/L) within 48 h or a change of >= 50% from the sCr baseline within 7 days. Only adult patients (age >=18) were included in the analysis. The patients with positive AKI on day 1 were excluded because our goal was to predict new AKI cases. Each patient cohort was ... labelled with the occurrence of AKI on days 2 or 3 as the outcome of the prediction. Baseline sCr 1: The minimum sCr value within the first 24-h of ICU admission.

label: aki_rahimi2023_b2
citation: Kamel Rahimi A, et al. BMC Med Inform Decis Mak. 2023;23:207. doi:10.1186/s12911-023-02306-0. Materials and methods.
text: We included patients with at least one sCr measurement on days 1, 2 and 3 following ICU admissions. We estimated AKI cases solely on the sCr criterion of the KDIGO definition defined as an increase in sCr of >= 0.3 mg/dL (26.5 umol/L) within 48 h or a change of >= 50% from the sCr baseline within 7 days. Only adult patients (age >=18) were included in the analysis. The patients with positive AKI on day 1 were excluded because our goal was to predict new AKI cases. Each patient cohort was ... labelled with the occurrence of AKI on days 2 or 3 as the outcome of the prediction. Baseline sCr 2: The pre-ICU baseline sCr was defined by using the MDRD backward calculation based on age and gender with an eGFR value of 75 ml/min/1.73 m2 (sCrGFR-75) to identify and exclude patients with AKI on day 1 of admission. The formula presented below represents the calculation of sCrGFR-75: SCr_GFR-75 = (75 / (186 * age^-0.203 * 0.742 [if female]))^-0.887. We then used the minimum creatine value on day 1 of admission as the baseline SCr.

label: aki_rahimi2023_b3
citation: Kamel Rahimi A, et al. BMC Med Inform Decis Mak. 2023;23:207. doi:10.1186/s12911-023-02306-0. Materials and methods.
text: We included patients with at least one sCr measurement on days 1, 2 and 3 following ICU admissions. We estimated AKI cases solely on the sCr criterion of the KDIGO definition defined as an increase in sCr of >= 0.3 mg/dL (26.5 umol/L) within 48 h or a change of >= 50% from the sCr baseline within 7 days. Only adult patients (age >=18) were included in the analysis. The patients with positive AKI on day 1 were excluded because our goal was to predict new AKI cases. Each patient cohort was ... labelled with the occurrence of AKI on days 2 or 3 as the outcome of the prediction. Baseline sCr 3: The pre-ICU baseline sCr was defined as the mean of all sCr values in the 180 to 7 days before ICU admissions. When baseline sCr was not available, the MDRD backward equation was calculated using age and gender to estimate baseline sCr (sCrGFR-75). The formula presented below represents the calculation of sCrGFR-75: SCr_GFR-75 = (75 / (186 * age^-0.203 * 0.742 [if female]))^-0.887.

label: readmit_gupta2022
citation: Gupta M, et al. Proc Mach Learn Res. 2022;193:311-325. Sections on prediction tasks and experiments.
text: Readmission tasks can be defined for readmission after user-defined (between 10 to 150) days from the previous admission discharge time. Task: implement the 30-day readmission label (the pipeline's default and the paper's example task), on hospital admissions.

label: readmit_prempeh2026
citation: Prempeh AGA, Tenfelde A. J Intensive Care Med. 2026;41(10):1008-1012. doi:10.1177/08850666261425613. Main Outcome and Measures.
text: The primary outcome was all-cause 90-day hospital readmission, defined as any subsequent admission occurring within 90 days of the index hospital discharge. Readmissions were identified by comparing the admission timestamp of subsequent encounters for the same patient to the discharge timestamp of the index hospitalization. Task: implement only this readmission rule, not the paper's postoperative ICU cohort.

label: readmit_shen2025
citation: Shen X, Yang J, Zhang X. J Thorac Dis. 2025;17(3):1207-1216. doi:10.21037/jtd-24-1738. Inclusion and exclusion criteria; Definitions.
text: Exclusion criteria: patients with multiple records of HF, patients who died in hospital, patients who lacked readmission time, patients whose readmission time was less than 1 day, and patients whose hospitalization time was less than 2 days. 90-day readmission: the patient was readmitted to the hospital within 90 days after discharge due to illness and other reasons. Task: implement the readmission rule and its death, readmission-time and hospitalization-time exclusions for all admissions, not the paper's heart-failure cohort.

label: ye2025_no_rule

text: The study included patients with diabetes who were at least 18 years old, admitted to the ICU for a minimum of 24 h, and had at least seven finger-stick blood glucose measurements recorded within a 24-hour ICU stay. Task: implement the 'patients with diabetes' criterion.

label: su2025_no_window
citation: Su H, et al. Brain Behav. 2025;15(10):e70958. doi:10.1002/brb3.70958. Methods.
text: ICU readmission was defined as a subsequent ICU admission after hospital discharge, triggered by a newly developed or recurrent medical condition. Patients who remained hospitalized and were transferred back to the ICU during the same index admission were not considered readmitted in this study.
